name: McCORMACK, the Hon. Michael Francis

headline.note: Private newspaper work is established from 1981 to 2002, followed by publishing in 2002–2010. Explicit full-time evidence now supports the initial cadetship, whose end is unknown; it is not extended to later roles. MSS legal entity and newspaper family control are documented. Unresolved boundaries, leave, later hours and overlaps prevent public/private full-time totals.

career_spells.employer: The Daily Advertiser / Riverina Media Group
career_spells.evidence_note: Official records give 1992–2002; Charles Sturt University archives corroborate the editor years, and contemporaneous ABC reporting places suspension and departure in February 2002. Exact appointment and cessation days, hours and leave remain unresolved. CSU archives support private family control during this employment; the 2007 Rural Press acquisition was later. A September 2003 ABC report confirms an out-of-court dismissal settlement, not continued work through that date. The member’s current general biography dates editorship to1991, whereas the detailed official chronology distinguishes acting1991–1992 from editor1992 onward. This may reflect compressed wording; preserve the detailed phases pending appointment records rather than silently changing the start.
career_spells.counting_note: The private-media employer and broad continuity are established, but mixed-precision boundaries and missing full-time evidence prevent an exact duration.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies and McCormack's published history record the group-editor appointment from 1996 within the continuing Daily Advertiser editorship. research_notes: The official newspaper chronology is preserved as sequential title spells; the group-editor role overlaps the Daily Advertiser editorship and is not double-counted.
The Daily Advertiser and Riverina Media Group are treated as private media employers at the time.
MSS is treated as private self-employment, but founding and publishing titles do not establish full-time work or exact continuity through the 2010 campaign.
Turf Club governance, party campaign roles, party office and federal elected office are separated and excluded under the codebook.
No private full-time total is calculated because exact boundaries, hours, leave and the substantive status of MSS remain unsupported.

2026-10-01 follow-up separates explicitly full-time cadetship from the broader official reporter interval, adds the earlier ground-announcer role and four sporting organisation roles, and identifies MSS company/ABN history. Election day is removed as an unsupported business cessation date.

Searched public professional posts, registry history, employer ownership archives, member career and first-speech material, exact newspaper entry/exit dates, business clients and dismissal reporting. Full-time evidence applies only to the initial cadetship. ABC’s original suspension page was inaccessible but its September 2003 settlement report was retrieved. An anniversary post with relative timestamp does not justify an exact start date. Unrelated namesakes and other workers’ full-time arrangements excluded.

Second follow-up2October2026: employer/cadetship, exact commencement, dismissal newsletters, company sale and client searches did not resolve cadetship completion, later full-time status or MSS cessation. The member’s general1991 editor wording is documented against the detailed acting/editor chronology; no new countable interval. UQ newspaper-history newsletters16/17 returned403 and were not retried. Public indexed snippets insufficient to identify exact suspension/dismissal dates. A15November1981 date in the member’s2020 sports interview dates league reorganisation, not his employment commencement. Relative forty-year anniversary remains insufficient for an exact start. No substantive new employment fact established; do not count this as materially enriched.
